children.value: > Fact From Story: The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.

> Fact From Story: A new class action lawsuit filed this week in the U.S. District Court in D.C. accuses Google and parent company Alphabet of anticompetitive behavior in violation of U.S. antitrust law, the Sherman Act, and others, on behalf of news publishers.
> > Fact From Story: The suit points to Google’s older question-and-answer technologies, like the “Knowledge Graph” launched in May 2012, as part of the problem.

> > > Fact From Story: Google compiled this massive database by extracting information from Publishers’ websites — what Google calls ‘materials shared across the web’ —and from ‘open source and licensed databases.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Extracting information from a source means to take information from that source.

> > Fact From Story: The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.
> > > Fact From Story: Some publishers are now trying to get ahead of the problem. | Fact From Story

> > > Fact From Story: The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google is “starving the free press” by sharing publishers’ content on Google, losing them “billions of dollars.” | Fact From Story
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: A publisher would not try to get ahead of a problem, unless there was a problem to get ahead of. | Commonsense Knowledge
> > Commonsense Knowledge: A case filed in court is a lawsuit.
> Commonsense Knowledge: A lawsuit is an accusation.
